messages:
customer_john: Hey team — our Private control plane is seeing intermittent mTLS handshake failures from a handful of corporate egress IPs since ~09:45 PDT. App logs show API errors and clients see connection resets. Error rate ~7%. Posting client-side openssl and control-plane logs.

maya_support: Sorry about that — can you paste the exact client error and any openssl/tcpdump output? Also which private endpoint hostname and what egress proxy are they using?

customer_john: Host: private-control.redwood.example.com. Egress proxy: corp-proxy.company.net:8443 (TLS inspection enabled). Client openssl output: 
```
openssl s_client -connect private-control.redwood.example.com:443 -servername private-control.redwood.example.com -alpn h2
...
SSL handshake has read 512 bytes and written 432 bytes
*** fatal alert: handshake_failure
```
Control plane log snippet: 
```
2026-03-16T16:45:12Z control-plane tls: mTLS handshake failed: peer cert CN mismatch, expected 'redwood-client', got 'corp-proxy'
```
We also noticed occasional ClientHello SNI being empty when traffic hits the NGFW.

maya_support: That suggests the proxy is either terminating TLS or mangling the ClientHello (SNI rewrite/truncation). If the proxy terminates and re-initiates TLS, it typically won't forward the original client cert for mTLS, so handshake to our control plane will fail. Can you run a direct s_client to the control-plane IP (bypass DNS) and then via corporate proxy to compare?

customer_john: Done. When we resolve directly to the backend IP it succeeds. When we go via the corporate proxy the handshake fails. So proxy is definitely in the path.

ricardo_netops: On some NGFWs the inspection engine either replaces SNI or truncates long hostnames. If SNI is rewritten to corp-proxy.company.net the control-plane picks the wrong cert chain. Do you have a pcap showing the ClientHello?

customer_john: We captured a small pcap (not pasted here) — tcpdump shows ClientHello SNI present from client, but after the NGFW the outbound ClientHello sometimes has SNI set to empty string or to corp-proxy.company.net. That correlates with failures.

oncall_marc: Paging runtime — could cert selection or SNI routing on our side be fragile if SNI is missing? @sre_bot any recent TLS config changes?

sre_bot: Runtime audit: no TLS cert bundle or SNI routing changes since 2026-03-10 03:21 UTC. No rollouts in the last 72h.

maya_support: Short repro steps for customer to validate and for vendor: 1) curl -v --resolve to hit specific backend IP, 2) openssl s_client with -servername to see handshake, 3) capture full ClientHello with tshark -V -x. Example commands: 
```
# direct to backend IP (bypass DNS)
curl -v --cert client.crt --key client.key --resolve private-control.redwood.example.com:443:10.0.5.12 https://private-control.redwood.example.com/healthz

# openssl debug
openssl s_client -connect private-control.redwood.example.com:443 -servername private-control.redwood.example.com -status -alpn h2
```
If the direct test succeeds and proxy test fails, proxy is the culprit.

ricardo_netops: We can open a change request to add a proxy exception for that host, but vendor may have a bug where long SNI is truncated and empty SNI falls back to default cert. Intermittency could be due to load balancing across inspection instances with different configs. I'll escalate to vendor and request a hotspot capture.

customer_john: One more detail — some client hosts show successful handshakes even via proxy. Our hypothesis: proxy sometimes preserves TLS passthrough (no inspection) for certain flows (maybe large MTU or unknown pattern) and sometimes inspects. So flights of success/failure.

maya_support: That matches an inspection cluster inconsistency. Two remediation paths: (A) Ask NetOps/vendor to allow TCP passthrough for private-control.* (no TLS inspection), which preserves client mTLS. (B) If passthrough is not possible, vendor would need to do mTLS bridging and forward client certs (rare). We strongly recommend (A) as the immediate fix.

ricardo_netops: I'll open the vendor ticket and temporary firewall exception. Also can enable IP-level allowlist from our egress CIDRs to the control-plane VIPs as a stopgap.

customer_john: Thanks — we've started a vendor ticket and will try the curl/openssl tests you provided. Will share captures.

maya_support: Also FYI — if SNI is being truncated, you may see the ClientHello length change; capture the first 256 bytes of the ClientHello to confirm truncation. If empty SNI is present, server will pick default cert and mTLS will obviously fail because CN/SAN won't match.

ricardo_netops: Noted. I'll push for an urgent exception.

customer_john: Opening internal ticket TKT-4532 and vendor case VND-9981. Will update when vendor responds. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

sre_bot: Incident created INC-2026-03-16-7734 and linked to TKT-4532.

maya_support: Keep this thread updated with vendor findings and packet captures. If you want a quick rule we can also provision an IP-based allowlist on our side — ping me after vendor confirms.

customer_john: Will do. Appreciated.
